title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Friday morning, Nov 20
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 7:25 AM ET Friday, Nov 20, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). The biggest mover overnight is a disinformation push on the Right: Tina Peters's attorney Peter Ticktin is urging Trump to 'nullify' the 2026 midterms, invoke the Insurrection Act and impose martial law before the new Congress is seated. That query matched 9,580 posts in 24 hours (3.44× its prior average; 5,948 overnight versus 1,418 a night earlier), the largest count this morning. The president has no power to cancel results or declare martial law, and fact-checkers found no evidence machines switched votes. On the Far Left, a 2023 clip of Mike Johnson, Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer chanting 'We stand with Israel' went viral again without its date (4,991 posts, 9.94×), as 'AIPAC Shakur' cooled to 2,756. Sen. Elissa Slotkin's endorsement of Chris Van Hollen pushed the Schumer challenge back up overnight (5,593 posts; 4,040 overnight versus 1,565). On the Right, the 'amnesty' frame on the Protect Our Neighbors Act held at 3,708 posts (3.31×), the Ian Murray noncitizen story doubled to 2,550, and popular-vote compact posts tripled overnight (2,618 versus 823). Two faded cards were dropped: Jeffries's ATM confrontation and 'Make America Nice Again.' Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this morning or carried over from last evening and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

trends.detail: U.S. trends were pulled at about 7:12 AM ET with x.get_trends_by_woeid (WOEID 23424977, max 50; 50 returned). K-pop voting tags (#VOTEFORBTS, 97,447 posts; #DAESANGFORBTS, 92,541), 'Signed' (98,428), 'Good Friday' (56,474), sports and entertainment dominated. 'Kasich' (2,386 posts) matches an X News story on John Kasich urging Republicans to drop MAGA; it is an intra-GOP fight, not an opposition narrative, so we did not score it. 'RED Friday' (3,651) and 'Remember Everyone Deployed' (no post count in the trend object) are the weekly troop-support tag, and 'Kyiv' (48,706) is foreign news. None of the trends matched a scored query, so no card received the trend bonus this morning. Where a trend object had no tweet_count, its volume is unavailable and we did not estimate it.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. This morning's top Right card is a call to overturn the election itself; it comes from a lawyer with access to Trump, not from party leaders, and we tag it Right because that is the audience pushing it. The 'We stand with Israel' video is shared by both the pro-Palestinian left and 'America First' accounts on the right; we tag it Far Left because its target is Democratic leadership. The Social Security card stays tagged Right because the 'Ponzi scheme' frame is a Right talking point, even though many posts matching it are backlash. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Friday, Nov 20, 2026, 7:25 AM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 7:12 AM ET. Last evening's snapshot (Nov 19, 5:30 PM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Fourteen of its sixteen narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps last evening's by 10 hours (7 AM to 5 PM ET Thursday), so we also report each query's 5 PM–7 AM ET overnight count against the same hours a night earlier. Two narratives were dropped because they faded: Jeffries's ATM confrontation (349 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.24× its prior daily average; 39 overnight versus 657 a night earlier) and 'Make America Nice Again' (132 posts, 0.78×). Two were added with new queries: Peter Ticktin's call to 'nullify' the midterms and the resurfaced 2023 'We stand with Israel' video. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: a broader Hasan Piker 'majority too big' query (373 posts, 1.89×), the House Republicans' 'Grand Theft Taxpayer' meme (339 posts in 24 hours, almost no baseline), noted on the tax card, and Rep. James Comer's 'investigations for TV' charge (155 posts), noted on the impeachment card. An earlier, narrower 'nullify' query that required Trump or Democrats terms matched fewer posts (993) and was replaced by the card's query. A query for the Democratic Governors Association's 'A woman's place is in the governor's mansion' post matched no posts, so that story is not scored.

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 8:00 AM ET Friday, Nov 13 (the earliest whole-hour start the recent-count API allowed at pull time), through 7:00 AM ET Friday, Nov 20. The last 24 hourly buckets (7:00 AM ET Thursday, Nov 19, through 7:00 AM ET Friday, Nov 20, exactly 24 hours) give the 24-hour count, and the whole window gives the 'seven-day' total. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved in this morning's searches and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, research groups, pollsters, bill trackers, blogs, X News summaries, and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets. We re-researched the Van Hollen, popular-vote compact and Ian Murray cards, plus the two new cards, and counted only outlets retrieved this morning on those cards, which is why some outlet counts changed (the Murray card keeps three: the Erie Times-News, retrieved this morning, plus WJET and The Center Square, retrieved again in this morning's search). For the other cards, which we did not re-research this morning, the outlet count is carried over from last evening, and each of those cards says so. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 7:12 AM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this morning. No card got the trend bonus this morning. The 'nullify,' Israel-video, Erie and immigration queries had low baselines earlier in the week, so their acceleration indices are maxed out. The Van Hollen and popular-vote queries carry last week's launch spikes in their seven-day totals, which keeps their acceleration low even though overnight volume rose. Read the post counts alongside the scores. Evening-to-morning score changes also reflect the higher volume ceiling (9,580 this morning versus 5,557 last evening) and how much coverage we retrieved.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The 'nullify' query overlaps the rigged-midterms query, and its seven-day total includes an earlier wave of matching posts from Nov. 14 to 16 that we did not review. The Israel-video, 'AIPAC Shakur,' Jeffries/AIPAC, Jeffries Iran funding and DSA queries share many speaker-race posts. The Social Security query also catches posts attacking Johnson. The immigration query includes the phrase 'Stephen A' with Democrats/immigration terms, so it can catch unrelated Stephen A. Smith posts. The Erie query includes the bare word 'Erie' with citizenship or voting terms, so it can catch unrelated Erie posts. The impeachment query also catches Democrats discussing impeachment. The rigged-midterms query also catches posts mocking fraud claims. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This morning we pulled fresh samples for the 'nullify,' Israel-video, Van Hollen, popular-vote compact and Erie queries. Other cards carry last evening's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this morning: 'Trump can nullify the midterms and declare martial law' is false; the president has no authority over state results and no law permits martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy), and Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org found no evidence that voting machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms. The viral 'We stand with Israel' clip of Johnson, Jeffries and Schumer is real but is from the Nov. 14, 2023, March for Israel, not a post-midterm pledge (AP). Carried over from last evening: posts using the Ian Murray case as proof that noncitizens are voting have no evidence behind them; 'The Protect Our Neighbors Act gives 1.6 million people green cards' is misleading; 'Democrats are already preparing a third impeachment' is a prediction by Jim Jordan, not a report; 'Pro-Israel money delivered Jeffries's 251-11 win' remains unproven, since the ballot was secret; CNBC's experts say the 'Ponzi scheme' label misses how Social Security is funded, and PolitiFact has rated the comparison False when others made it; 'Pressley's H.R. 40 pays reparations' is misleading; 'Democrats are importing voters' runs into the law, since noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections; 'Jeffries backs the Iran war' is false as stated; 'Democrats will defund the military to shut down the government' is misleading; and Lead Stories found no '30,000-case' Texas voter fraud probe.

narratives.title: NEW: 'Nullify the midterms' — Tina Peters's lawyer urges Trump to void the results, invoke the Insurrection Act and impose martial law
narratives.query: (Ticktin OR ((nullify OR nullified OR "martial law" OR "Insurrection Act") (midterms OR midterm OR "2026 election" OR "election results"))) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Urgent and conspiratorial ('CALL TO ACTION'); copy-paste campaigns aimed at the White House
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday, the Gateway Pundit's post on the story led by far (@gatewaypundit, 4,239 likes, 1,930 reposts, 89,762 views), followed by @DavidJHarrisJr ('BREAKING: Peter Ticktin… is calling on President Trump to nullify the results,' 2,044 likes, 16,632 views) and @GailGolec's 'CALL TO ACTION' (276 likes). Dozens of small accounts pasted the same 'BREAKING' text, tagged @POTUS, or posted the White House phone number ('NULLIFY THE MIDTERMS!!!!!! WE ALL KNOW THEY WERE STOLEN!!'). We saw almost no pushback inside this query's top results. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this morning. The query matched 9,580 posts in the last 24 hours (3.44× its prior daily average), the largest count in this snapshot, and 26,296 over seven days; 5,948 came from 5 PM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday, versus 1,418 in the same hours a night earlier. Florida attorney Peter Ticktin, lead counsel for convicted former Colorado clerk Tina Peters and a friend of Trump's from New York Military Academy, called on Trump to declare the 2026 state and federal results void, invoke the Insurrection Act, which he said would bring martial law, and act before the new Congress is seated on Jan. 3; he urged supporters to call the White House. His claim rests on the idea that algorithms switched votes. He has floated this before: before the election he told MS NOW that Trump should be ready to 'enter an emergency order that basically would be tantamount to martial law,' and The Independent, citing Axios, reported he said on a Sept. 30 call that 'there would have to be martial law' after 'another rigged election.' We found no reporting that the White House has acted on the demand. The query overlaps the rigged-midterms card, and its seven-day total also includes an earlier wave of matching posts from Nov. 14 to 16 that we did not review.
talkingPoints: The 2026 midterms were rigged by algorithms.
Trump must void the results before Jan. 3, or 'there's no coming back.'
Invoke the Insurrection Act; call the White House and demand it.
If Democrats are seated, they will remove Trump and Vance.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: The Gateway Pundit (@gatewaypundit, 89,762 views on its post), @DavidJHarrisJr (16,632 views), @GailGolec, @jimhoft_, and many small accounts posting identical 'BREAKING' copy and the White House switchboard number. Origin: attorney Peter Ticktin (@PeterTicktin). Election-skeptic allies Tina Peters and Mike Lindell have pushed related federal-intervention ideas (MS NOW).
narratives.whyItWorks: It gives voters who cannot accept a blue wave a deadline (Jan. 3), a remedy (one presidential order) and a task (call the White House), which turns grievance into action. It comes from someone with real access: Ticktin says he knows Trump from their teens and has been in the Oval Office with Peters (MS NOW). And it builds on months of vote-switching rumors that fact-checkers have already debunked but that many in the audience never saw corrected.
narratives.audience: Hard-core 'stolen election' believers, Tina Peters supporters, Gateway Pundit and Telegram/Gab audiences, and older conservative voters primed by the 2020 fight.
narratives.counter: Say it plainly and calmly: the president has no power to cancel state election results, and no law lets him declare martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy). The Insurrection Act lets troops help enforce the law, not overturn it, and federal law bars troops at polling places. On 'algorithms': Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org found no evidence that machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms; the reports traced to touchscreen errors that voters could correct. Point out that Republicans won races on the same machines. Don't amplify the phone-number campaign.

factChecks.claim: The president can nullify the 2026 midterm results and declare martial law.
factChecks.detail: The Constitution gives the president no power over how states run or certify elections, and no statute authorizes martial law. The Insurrection Act permits troop deployments to enforce the law, not to change results, and federal law bars armed federal officers at the polls. This row relies on legal analyses from the Brennan Center and Protect Democracy; it is not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Voting machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms.
factChecks.detail: Snopes found no evidence machines switched votes in either direction during the 2026 midterms; the reports it reviewed likely reflected human error or touchscreen alignment problems, and voters can review selections before casting. PolitiFact and FactCheck.org reached similar conclusions in October. Ticktin's specific 'algorithm' claim was not separately rated.

Name who it was written for: a 73-year-old grandmother who checked in with ICE for 30 years. factChecks.claim: The Protect Our Neighbors Act gives green cards to 1.6 million people with deportation orders.
factChecks.detail: The bill's sponsor puts the number of people with final removal orders at about 1.19 million; 1.6 million is an earlier ICE figure. The bill would let an order expire only after 10 years, allow a judge to renew it, and let a person petition for any status they are eligible for only after 10 years of continuous presence and no conviction for a crime punishable by more than a year. It does not hand out green cards automatically, and it has no path in the current Republican House. This is TDDR's read of the bill text and Simon's release, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: The Protect Our Neighbors Act would wipe out 1.6 million deportation orders.
factChecks.detail: About 1.6 million people have final removal orders (ICE testimony cited by ABC News), but the bill covers only orders at least 10 years old for people continuously present with no criminal conviction, and a judge could renew an order. No count of who would qualify has been published. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Iowa and Texas results prove the 2026 midterms were rigged.

factChecks.claim: Texas Democrats 'found' 20 million new votes to flip the state blue.

talkingPoints: 251-11 is what AIPAC money buys.
He calls Jerusalem New York's 'sixth borough' and wants to be your speaker.
The 11 'no' votes are the only Democrats who listened to voters.
1.2 million people signed to replace him and the caucus ignored them.
Unity means falling in line behind the donors.
narratives.amplifiers: Left: @codepink and co-founder Medea Benjamin; @TheTNHoller's clip (1,780 likes, 35,565 views); @trtworld; Common Dreams. Pushback: commentators cited by X News, including Shermichael Singleton and Paul Begala, who called some nicknames racist; Daily Kos argued the 'haters are mainly online.'
narratives.whyItWorks: A lopsided, secret-ballot vote is easy to read as insiders protecting their own, and the AIPAC money gives the left a single, concrete villain for every disappointment, from Gaza to Iran to Medicare for All. The 11 named no votes make the resistance look real and organized, and the petition number makes it feel like the base was overruled.
narratives.audience: Progressive and pro-Palestinian activists, DSA and Justice Democrats networks, young left voters who drove the midterm wave, and left media audiences (CODEPINK, Truthout, Breaking Points-style shows). The Right reshares it as a 'Democratic civil war.'
narratives.counter: Lead with the incoming progressives' own words: they say talks with Jeffries are producing 'meaningful progress' and are ongoing. Point to concrete wins (AOC leading the healthcare working group, a promised early war-powers vote) and separate verified money figures from inflated ones: OpenSecrets data show far less from AIPAC itself than the viral totals. Don't call critics racist by default; argue the record.

factChecks.claim: The petition to replace Jeffries has 1.2 million verified signatures.
factChecks.rating: Unverified — signatures are not verified voters
factChecks.detail: Democracy Now! and Newsweek reported the Change.org petition passed one million signatures on Nov. 9. Posts and X News summaries Wednesday cite 1.2 million; we still could not verify that number. Change.org does not verify that signers are voters or constituents. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Hakeem Jeffries has taken $1.5 million from AIPAC.
factChecks.detail: Per OpenSecrets data reported by Newsweek: $49,565 in contributions facilitated through AIPAC and $11,700 directly from AIPAC's PAC in the 2025–26 cycle; $1,741,230 from the broader pro-Israel category (PACs and individuals) through 2024, which is not an AIPAC-only total. Sludge reported AIPAC PAC sent $149,300 earmarked by one donor to his joint fundraising committee in May. OpenSecrets cautions these figures should not be added together. The $1.5 million figure in posts traces to Track AIPAC, per Middle East Eye. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Pro-Israel members' votes delivered Jeffries the nomination.
factChecks.detail: AP, NBC News and NPR report the 251-11 vote was a closed-door, secret ballot. Only 7 of the 11 opponents identified themselves, in a joint statement. No tally by member exists, so posts naming which members put him over the top are guesses. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

narratives.whyItWorks: Affordability won Democrats the midterms, so 'they'll raise your taxes' attacks the brand at its strongest point. It's also partly true — Democrats are debating tax increases — which makes the exaggeration ('on Americans') harder to rebut in one line.
narratives.audience: Conservative and libertarian voters, small-business owners, and swing voters who backed Democrats on costs. Also likely to resonate with moderate Democrats wary of the party's left.
narratives.counter: Say who pays. The proposals on the table target incomes over roughly $1 million and corporations, and Trump can veto all of it until 2029. Put the trade on the table plainly: restoring Medicaid, SNAP, and ACA subsidies for working families, paid for by the top bracket. Don't deny that a debate over tax increases is happening — it is.

factChecks.claim: Democrats are planning 'major tax hikes on Americans' for 2027.
factChecks.detail: The Wall Street Journal report, as quoted by Political Wire, says Democrats are 'weighing when to attach tax increases' to bills reversing Medicaid, SNAP, and health-subsidy cuts — a debate, not a passed plan. The Tax Foundation says the proposals on the table target high-income individuals and corporations and that any tax increase is 'limited by President Trump’s veto.' Viral posts dropped both caveats. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.
